clue.text: Jamaican was venal — black money of old was foremost

parts.note: B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
an obol was a small silver coin of ancient Greece
to have led is to have been in front

explanation.surface: A sketch of colonial corruption, where bribe money once came first.
explanation.walkthrough: BOBOL is Jamaican and Caribbean English for petty fraud or graft, and it can be used as a verb, so the past tense doubles the L.
explanation.definitionFit: To bobol is to practise corruption or embezzlement in Jamaican usage, so the past tense means behaved venally.

clue.text: Herring boat, v-vessel you rarely see capsizing?

indicators.note: a down entry that capsizes is turned upside down, so its letters run the other way

parts.note: a vessel rarely seen is a submarine; the stammered 'v-v' doubles its first letter

explanation.surface: A fishing boat so rarely seen that it might have capsized.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'v-vessel' mimics a stammer, so the short word for a submarine gets its first letter doubled before it is turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: A buss is a broad two- or three-masted Dutch fishing vessel formerly used in the herring fishery.

clue.text: In Old Testament book — it is about Egypt — one chronicles bygone lives

indicators.note: what follows is placed in the Testament, so those words sit inside

parts.note: OT is the usual abbreviation for the Old Testament
B is the abbreviation for book

indicators.note: one phrase goes about, that is around, the country, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written
the United Arab Republic, Egypt's official name from 1958 to 1971

explanation.surface: A biblical scholar notes that a book of the Old Testament mentions Egypt and records ancient lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Testament book' wants to be a single book such as Exodus, but the testament and the book are separate pieces. Egypt's old name as the United Arab Republic dates from its brief union with Syria.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituarist writes obituaries, the newspaper notices that record the lives of people who have recently died.

clue.text: Very skimpy waistcoat starts to rip open below trunk

indicators.note: in a down entry what is below comes underneath, so the letters it governs are placed second

parts.note: a bole is the trunk of a tree

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the opening letter of each of these two words

explanation.surface: A tiny waistcoat is about to split under someone's torso.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'below' puts the second piece under the first, so the trunk word comes on top. 'Trunk' suggests the body; it is the tree's.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolero is a very short open jacket or waistcoat ending above the waist, as worn in Spanish dress.

clue.text: Medicinal tea plant filled umpteen bags

indicators.note: to bag is to hold within, so the phrase before it holds the answer inside

parts.note: the run of letters across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A herbal tea plant has been packed into countless teabags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' looks like teabags, a noun; it is a verb meaning contains.
explanation.definitionFit: Ledum is the genus of Labrador tea, a shrub whose leaves were brewed as a tea and used in folk medicine.

clue.text: Old-style relay runner, lean, taking in morning walk

indicators.note: to take in is to admit within, so the following words go inside

parts.note: a ship lists when it leans to one side
AM, ante meridiem, is the abbreviation for morning
to pad is to walk steadily, as on foot

explanation.surface: A thin athlete of a bygone era goes for a morning stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: The ancient Greek torch race passed a lit torch from runner to runner, the original relay.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampadist was a runner in the lampadedromy, the ancient Greek torch race, a relay passing a flame between runners.

clue.text: Fool having wallop on drunken binge

parts.note: a ding is a blow or knock
a bat is a spree, as in 'on a bat', slang for a drinking bout

explanation.surface: A fool who has taken a thump while out on a bender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the blow on top of the binge in a down entry; 'wallop' also suggests beer, a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Dingbat is informal for a stupid or eccentric person, an idiot.

clue.text: What is exciting Mahdi's ——? Muhammad is

definitions.text: What is exciting Mahdi's ——? Muhammad is

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken letter for letter, as the full stock of letters
these letters are struck out of the stock, leaving the blank's word

explanation.surface: A riddle: what stirs up the Mahdi's people? The Prophet does.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as an equation: the letters of Mahdi's plus the missing word, stirred up, make Muhammad is. Take Mahdi's out of Muhammad is and four letters remain. The whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The umma is the worldwide community of Muslims, the body of believers whom the Mahdi would lead and whom the Prophet's message inspires.

clue.text: Open house (no moderation) receives indefinite number with endless beer

indicators.note: what receives something takes it inside, so the number goes within
'no' says the bracketed word is to be left out of the one before it

parts.note: taken as written, before part is removed
ho is an old word for a limit or moderation, as in 'out of all ho'
n stands for an unspecified number in mathematics

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: An open house where drinking is unrestrained, with a crowd and beer running out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open house' reads as a phrase, but 'Open' alone is the definition. HO, meaning stopping or moderation, is old and rare; removing it from house leaves USE.
explanation.definitionFit: To unseal something is to open it by breaking or removing its seal.

clue.text: Some awful old grimaces

indicators.note: something awful is in a bad way, so the letters are put into disorder

parts.note: taken letter for letter, as material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A few of the grimaces were dreadful old faces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like a quantifier for the grimaces, but its four letters are the material to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Moe is an obsolete spelling of mow, a wry face or grimace, so the plural fits the old sense.

clue.text: Get tight going wild in Tangiers

indicators.note: running wild means out of control, so the letters break rank

parts.note: taken letter for letter, as material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A tourist gets drunk while running riot in a Moroccan port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get tight' suggests getting drunk; it means drawing together or contracting.
explanation.definitionFit: To astringe is to bind or contract tissues, making them tighter, the action of an astringent.

clue.text: Sycophantic old louse, slippery with a strong drink inside

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old

indicators.note: the drink is placed within the other letters, so these words call for an insertion
something slippery will not hold still, so the letters slide out of their order

parts.note: taken letter for letter, as material to rearrange
a + gin, a strong spirit

explanation.surface: Contempt for a slimy old flatterer with a stiff drink in him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slippery' looks like a description of the louse, but it is the signal to rearrange; the drink sits inside the rearranged letters, not at an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleaginous literally means oily, and figuratively describes someone unctuously fawning, a sycophant's manner.

clue.text: Be a tenant having pound accepted as deposit

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a sitting tenant sits, occupying the property
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A tenant pays a pound into a deposit scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposit' looks like a rental deposit; it is the sediment a river leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Silt is fine sediment carried by water and laid down as a deposit on river beds and estuaries.

clue.text: Throw nuts randomly, each caught

indicators.note: something caught is held inside, so one piece is put within the other
done at random, so the letters fall in no fixed order

parts.note: taken letter for letter, as material to rearrange
EA is the standard abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: Someone tossing nuts about, catching one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw' reads as tossing nuts; it is the rider's sense, as a horse throws its rider.
explanation.definitionFit: To unseat is to throw a rider from the saddle, just as a bucking horse throws someone.

clue.text: Favour competitive run after part of play fog ruined (10, three words)

indicators.note: what comes after is placed later, so the contest word goes to the end

parts.note: an act is a main division of a play

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters lie in a broken order

parts.note: taken letter for letter, as material to rearrange
a race is a contest of speed

explanation.surface: A sporting fixture rearranged after fog spoiled part of a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' sets the race behind the rest in the final order, though it comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An act of grace is a favour or privilege granted freely rather than as of right, such as a general pardon.

clue.text: Come forward for increase

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to volunteer, step out of the line
second meaning: to raise the level or intensity

explanation.surface: A call for volunteers to come forward and get a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to volunteer by moving forward and to raise or intensify something.

clue.text: Current Labour MP, upright member touring our community in 'buggy'?

parts.note: the ins are the party in office, which Labour was when this appeared in 2010; current also means in

indicators.note: to tour a place is to travel around it, so one piece encircles the other

parts.note: a stile is an upright piece in a door or window frame
the European Community, which Britain then belonged to

explanation.surface: A sitting MP touring a constituency in a little vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buggy' looks like a small car; in quotes with a question mark it means bug-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Insectile means of or like an insect, which is what a playful sense of buggy would mean.

clue.text: One skilled aboard masoolah getting tan round farm at sea

indicators.note: the tan word goes around the other letters, so it surrounds them

parts.note: to sun oneself is to tan

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: taken letter for letter, as material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A boatman sunbathing on deck while the craft passes a coastal farm.
explanation.walkthrough: A masoolah is a light Indian surf boat from the Coromandel coast. Here the tan word is split, with the rearranged farm letters going inside it before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfman is a sailor skilled in handling boats through surf, the very job on a masoolah, a surf boat.

clue.text: Sizeable addition to opening stake? (Turn off TV, please!)

indicators.note: a turn sends things off their course, so the letters are spun round

parts.note: taken letter for letter, as material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A gambler asks for the television to be switched off while raising the stakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed plea looks like an aside; its letters are the material and 'Turn off' says to rearrange them.
explanation.definitionFit: In the card game basset a septleva was a winning increase to seven times the original stake, a large addition.

clue.text: Time in E. Asian island? Try this curry dish

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other, so this word asks for an insertion

parts.note: Bali is an Indonesian island
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A travel tip: on an Asian island, try the local curry.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside BALI; balti is a Birmingham-born curry, not Balinese, which is the surface's misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a spicy curry cooked and served in a wok-like metal bowl, popular in British curry houses.

clue.text: Older man's potty, aka blueback (9, two words)

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters go mad and change places

parts.note: taken letter for letter, as material to rearrange

explanation.surface: An elderly man is called potty, otherwise known by an odd nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: Azed spells out the enumeration because the answer is two words; 'aka' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Blueback is another name for the sockeye, a Pacific salmon species whose flesh is deep red.

clue.text: Solitaire getting you to relax in middle of week

indicators.note: one piece is put in the other, so it goes inside
only the central letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the two letters at the centre of this four-letter word
remit, as an instruction to you, means relax or slacken

explanation.surface: A card game of patience helps someone unwind midweek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solitaire' suggests the card game; it is a person who lives alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a hermit, a religious recluse, and a solitaire is an old word for one who lives in solitude.

clue.text: To snoop round toper I abused seemliness

indicators.note: the snooping word goes round the rest, enclosing it

parts.note: to pry is to snoop

indicators.note: misused or mistreated, so the letters are knocked out of shape

parts.note: taken letter for letter, as material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A busybody snoops round a drunkard, scorning lack of decorum.
explanation.walkthrough: A toper is a habitual drinker; the word survives mostly in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Propriety is conformity to accepted standards of behaviour, the quality of being seemly or proper.

clue.text: First mate going round the perimeter?

indicators.note: the friend word goes round the other, surrounding it

parts.note: a pal is a mate, a friend
a rim is an outer edge

explanation.surface: A ship's first mate makes a circuit of the deck's edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First mate' reads as a ship's officer; the two words split, one the definition and one the friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Primal means original or first in time, as in a primal instinct.

clue.text: Primitive types join coach wanting lift north

indicators.note: in a down entry a lift raises the letters upward, so they read bottom to top

parts.note: to embus is to board a bus or coach
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Uncouth types climb on a coach, wanting a ride north.
explanation.walkthrough: EMBUS, a military word for getting troops onto vehicles, is flipped and then N is added at the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Submen are people of a lower, less developed type than normal humans, primitive beings.

clue.text: Volume of liquor added. 'Not so generous,' does one hear?

indicators.note: asks what is heard, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: tighter means meaner; in non-rhotic British speech the two words match

explanation.surface: A barman topping up a drink is accused of stinginess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquor' means a solution in chemistry, not a spirit; the measure is from titration.
explanation.definitionFit: In titration the titre is the volume of standard solution added from the burette to complete the reaction.

clue.text: Self-catering with red wine for local crowd

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation used in holiday listings for self-catering
rouge is French for red, as in vin rouge

explanation.surface: A self-catering holiday with red wine to share among locals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crowd' reads as a noun for a gathering of locals; it is a verb, and 'local' marks a dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrouge is a dialect verb meaning to squeeze or press, to crowd someone.

clue.text: Double star: in 'foot' of Centaur I lie (viewed from below)

indicators.note: the foot of a word in a down entry is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of this word
taken as written

indicators.note: seen from beneath, a down word reads upward, from its end

parts.note: lig is a dialect word for lie

explanation.surface: Astronomy: a double star lies at the foot of the constellation Centaurus.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes round 'foot' point to the name's meaning: Rigil Kentaurus is Arabic for the foot of the Centaur. The surface fact is literally true.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigil, also Rigil Kentaurus, is Alpha Centauri, a bright binary or double star in the Centaur's foot.

clue.text: Line unknown in e.g. Faerie Queene? The reverse

indicators.note: asks for the letters to be read in the opposite direction
one pair of letters sits inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: the abbreviation for 'for example', taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A literary puzzle about an untraced line in Spenser's epic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'e.g.' looks like 'for example' introducing the poem, but its letters are taken literally. The definition is the hazy part: this reads Faerie Queene as pointing to Spenser's spelling of guile.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyle is taken here as an archaic spelling of guile, the sort found in Spenser's deliberately old-fashioned verse; elsewhere it means a brewing of wort.

clue.text: Sound quality: possibly deal for listeners

indicators.note: addressed to the ear, so the word counts only by how it sounds

parts.note: deal is pine or fir wood, an example of timber; 'possibly' marks the example

explanation.surface: A note on how a sound comes across, perhaps a business deal pitched to an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' wants to be a bargain; it is softwood plank. The two words sound alike in non-rhotic British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbre is the characteristic tone colour that distinguishes one voice or instrument from another at the same pitch.

clue.text: Potentate, part in Semiramide?

indicators.note: a part lies within the whole, so the word is found inside the next one

parts.note: letters two to five of the opera's title

explanation.surface: A ruler takes a role in Rossini's opera Semiramide, about a Babylonian queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' suggests an operatic role, which suits the surface, but it marks a run of letters inside the title.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or prince, a potentate holding power over a state or people.

clue.text: Wandering in ME city, concerned with roots

indicators.note: roaming off course, so the letters stray from their order

parts.note: taken letter for letter, as material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A genealogist roams a city in Maine, tracing family roots.
explanation.walkthrough: ME is the postal code for Maine; the surface pictures ancestry, but the roots are those of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Etymic relates to an etymon, the original root form from which a word is derived.

clue.text: Muslim leader: what'll one say, denying he's PM?

parts.note: speaking of oneself, one says 'I'm'
the opposite of p.m., afternoon, is a.m., morning

explanation.surface: A cleric asked to deny being the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like Prime Minister; it is post meridiem, the afternoon, so the denial is 'I'm a.m.'
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque and can also be a title for a Muslim religious leader.

clue.text: Make delicate slice of artichoke with sesame in chopped olives

indicators.note: cut up, so the letters are diced and remixed
a slice is a small piece, here the opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of this vegetable
til is the sesame plant
taken letter for letter, as material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A recipe: a delicate starter of artichoke and sesame mixed into chopped olives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make delicate' sounds like cooking; it means to make light and airy. Til is the Indian name for sesame.
explanation.definitionFit: To volatilise is to make volatile, light and evanescent, turning a substance airy or vaporous.

clue.text: Cut length short? It involves switching blades

parts.note: to axe is to cut
L is the short form of length

explanation.surface: Trimming a length shorter needs scissors, whose blades switch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blades' suggests cutting tools, fitting the surface; they are skate blades.
explanation.definitionFit: An axel is a figure-skating jump that takes off from one skate and lands on the other, changing feet in the air.

clue.text: Observe what goes in bin — tears may ruin it

parts.note: to eye is to observe
a bin liner is the bag fitted inside a rubbish bin

explanation.surface: Watch what is thrown away, since rips can spoil a bin bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' first reads as rips in a bin bag; they are the crying kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeliner is make-up drawn along the eyelids, which weeping smears and spoils.
